method: Decode source WAV and rendered MP4 to 24000 Hz mono float PCM using Docker ffmpeg. Search full-scene correlation over +/- 1 second, refine to one sample, then compare multiple windows at the discovered common offset.

control.description: Encode the first original WAV directly to 48000 Hz stereo AAC using ffmpeg, then decode with the same PCM method.

conclusion: The rendered MP4 has a real constant 42.667 ms audio delay relative to the locked scene positions, not a generic ffmpeg decoder artifact. All three source voices match strongly after the same shift, with no observed cumulative timing drift. This shift equals two 1024-sample AAC packets at 48000 Hz and is consistent with encoder priming/mux timing, but the exact internal Remotion cause was not proven. The initial +/- 10 ms QA search could not reach this matching offset.
